disclosure: Context management: to save tokens, the harness omits parts of earlier tool outputs that already appear elsewhere and folds steps you have marked STALE. Every omission is marked by a `[context-manager]` note, which is NOT a shell error: it says what was omitted and where the same content still is. The bash command `restore <step>` shows the original agent message and tool observation for that step again exactly as first shown, without running anything; re-running the original command shows its current state instead. Trust the provided context and proceed; restore or re-run only when the omitted output is necessary for your next step, since each one adds a step and token tax.
disclosure_irreversible: Context management: to save tokens, the harness omits parts of earlier tool outputs that already appear elsewhere and folds steps you have marked STALE. Every omission is marked by a `[context-manager]` note, which is NOT a shell error: it says what was omitted and where the same content still is. Trust the provided context and proceed; re-run a command only when the omitted output is necessary for your next step, since each one adds a step and token tax.
protocol:
Begin every response with these two lines, then your reasoning and your bash tool call:
  PROGRESS: <one short line on what THIS step does>
  STALE: <step numbers whose output you will not read again, or `-` if none>
Each earlier tool output is labeled `[step N]`.
STALE is about OUTPUT you are finished reading, not about the action. Name a step once you have taken what you needed from its output and will not consult that text again: you read a file and drew your conclusion, a search led nowhere, a check ruled a guess out.
Do NOT name a step whose output you will still consult: the file you are about to change, the test results you are working against, the read that pinned down the root cause. Never name the step you are writing right now, it has no result yet.
Name steps AS SOON AS you are done with them. {window}
Named steps are folded into a `[context-manager]` note that keeps their PROGRESS lines and a signature skeleton.{restore}
Example first lines:
  PROGRESS: reading serializer.py to find the encode path
  STALE: 3, 4
These two lines are metadata, never let them replace your bash tool call.
protocol_window: Only the last {k} step{plural} before this one can still be named; older numbers are ignored, so saving up a big cleanup for later is wasted.
protocol_window_any: Any earlier step can still be named.
protocol_restore: To see a folded or omitted output again, run `restore <step>` as your bash command (for example `restore 7` or `restore 3-5`): it shows the output exactly as first shown and runs nothing. Re-run the original command instead when you need its current state.
remind_gentle:
[context-manager] Your last response did not start with the two metadata lines. Start this one with them, then continue:
  PROGRESS: <one short line on what THIS step does>
  STALE: <step numbers you are done with, or `-`>
remind_harsh: [context-manager] FORMAT VIOLATION ({misses} in a row): every response MUST start with the PROGRESS and STALE lines. Write them FIRST, before anything else, right now.
note_read: [context-manager] {path}:{start}-{end} omitted: identical to step {first}. `restore {step}` shows it again.
note_search: [context-manager] search output omitted: identical to step {first}. `restore {step}` shows it again.
note_output: [context-manager] output omitted: identical to step {first}. `restore {step}` shows it again.
note_partial: [context-manager] lines already shown at earlier steps are omitted below. `restore {step}` shows all of it again.
note_pytest: [context-manager] {omitted} of {total} lines omitted: passing tests, progress dots and warnings. `restore {step}` shows them again.
note_tests: [context-manager] passing and progress lines omitted. `restore {step}` shows them again.
restore_head: [context-manager] step {step} as first shown: its agent message, command and tool observation. Re-run the command for its current state.
restore_shown: [context-manager] step {step} is shown in full above: nothing to restore.
restore_invalid: [context-manager] no step {step}: steps so far are 0-{last}.
restore_cap: [context-manager] at most {max} steps per restore: the others were not restored.
